rule: The timing profiles a staging chain is built with (node/tools/mainnet-preparation/staging_chain.py --timings). Each profile replaces only the E05 values it lists; every other value is the production value. A run record lists its profile, each replaced value beside its production value, and the derived values.
block_seconds_basis: The approved 5-second block target, from which the evidence and margin seconds follow (E05 values lifecycle.*).
backup_interval_basis: The sentry's backup timer runs hourly with up to 15 minutes' random delay (host_files.py BACKUP_TIMER), so the newest off-host copy can be a snapshot interval plus 75 minutes old.
restore_trust_basis: A restore trusts the copy's header for the evidence age less a fourteenth of it (dytallix-pqc-engine restore.go; P01, 8 and 12 October 2026).
fault_recovery_target_basis: The fault injector's acceptance (T5): the sentry must catch back up to the validator within 120 seconds after a transient fault clears. The staging drill measured 13 to 21 seconds, so this is about six times the observed worst case (roughly two dozen 5-second block intervals). This is the rehearsal acceptance for transient faults only; it is stricter than and distinct from the six-hour per-host readiness catch-up budget (E05 catch_up_millis) used by the supervisor for a node rejoining from far behind. P01, 13 October 2026; launch/approvals/P01_E05_FAULT_RECOVERY_2026-10-13.json.
validator_restart_target_basis: The validator process restart's acceptance (T5, R02): blocks again within 5 minutes of a validator process restart, read on the sentry's public status page as the first block made after the restart. The simulation plan's approved recovery threshold (P01, 11 October 2026; launch/approvals/P01_T06_SIMULATION_PLAN_2026-10-11.json, "blocks again within 5 minutes of a validator process restart"), recorded here as a number; with one validator the chain halts while it is down, so this is the time from the restart to the next block.
host_loss_target_basis: Host loss's acceptance (T5): after the sentry's machine is powered off hard and on again on the same disk, its public status page serves a block made after the power-on within 10 minutes. This covers the boot, the node's start and its catch-up, so it is looser than the 120-second transient-fault target and the 5-minute validator restart. P01, 9 November 2026; launch/approvals/P01_T05_HOST_LOSS_2026-11-09.json.

production.use: R07, the dress rehearsal, and production: the exact approved values.

rehearsal.use: R01 to R06, so each lifecycle completes inside its 24-hour run.

ci.use: The CI staging network's kit replacement drill: a notice of 20 blocks; its snapshot interval is given on the command line. Its flood campaign: an admission queue of 64 entries, so a transaction flood can fill it from one runner (the production bound is 2,000).
